item.title: Arista EOS Tunnel Decapsulation Protocol-Type Bypass — CVE-2026-7473
item.description:
Metadata

Field Value
Date Added 2026-07-05
Last Updated 2026-06
Author / Researcher fevar54
CVE / Advisory CVE-2026-7473
Category network
Severity Medium
CVSS Score 5.8 (CVSSv3.1: AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:N/I:L/A:N); CVSSv4: 6.8
Status PoC
Tags arista, eos, vxlan, gre, gue, ipip, nvgre, tunnel-decapsulation, cwe-1023, packet-crafting
Related N/A

Affected Target

Field Value
Software / System Arista EOS (switches configured as tunnel decapsulation endpoints: VXLAN VTEP, GRE tunnel interface, or ip decap-group)
Versions Affected EOS 4.36.x, 4.35.x, 4.34.x, 4.33.x, 4.32.x, 4.31.x, 4.30.x, and earlier trains, per source repository. 7020R, 7280R/R2, and 7500R/R2 series fully affected; 7280R3, 7500R3, and 7800R3 series have limited exposure (IP-in-IPv6, GUEv6)
Language / Platform Python 3 (scapy-based packet crafting)
Authentication Required No
Network Access Required Yes — attacker must be able to send crafted IP packets to the switch’s configured decapsulation IP

Summary

Arista EOS switches configured as a tunnel decapsulation endpoint (for VXLAN, GRE, or generic ip decap-group/GUE/IP-in-IP profiles) incorrectly decapsulate and forward tunneled packets of an unexpected/non-configured protocol type as long as the outer destination IP matches the switch’s configured decapsulation IP. Because the switch does not verify that the tunnel protocol type matches what was actually configured (CWE-1023: Incomplete Comparison with Missing Factors), an attacker can send GRE traffic to a VXLAN-only endpoint (or vice versa), as well as IP-in-IP, NVGRE, and GUE traffic, and have it decapsulated and forwarded onto the internal network — bypassing the intended tunnel-type isolation.
